54: - $H_1 = a_1^+ a_1^- + b_1^+ b_1^-$

157: ### 2. Generator Label Convention
158: 
159: Following the B(0,n) label scheme, the proposed C(n+1) labels are:
160: 
161: | Root | Label | Oscillator realization |
162: |---|---|---|
163: | $\varepsilon + \delta_k$ | `E_eps_del{k}_pp` | $a_1^+ b_k^+$ |
164: | $\varepsilon - \delta_k$ | `E_eps_del{k}_pm` | $a_1^+ b_k^-$ |
165: | $-\varepsilon + \delta_k$ | `E_eps_del{k}_mp` | $a_1^- b_k^+$ |
166: | $-\varepsilon - \delta_k$ | `E_eps_del{k}_mm` | $a_1^- b_k^-$ |
167: | $2\delta_k$ | `E_2del{k}_p` | $\tfrac{1}{2}(b_k^+)^2$ |
168: | $-2\delta_k$ | `E_2del{k}_m` | $\tfrac{1}{2}(b_k^-)^2$ |
169: | $\delta_i + \delta_j$ ($i<j$) | `E_del{i}_del{j}_pp` | $b_i^+ b_j^+$ |
170: | $\delta_i - \delta_j$ ($i<j$) | `E_del{i}_del{j}_pm` | $b_i^+ b_j^-$ |
171: | $-\delta_i + \delta_j$ ($i<j$) | `E_del{i}_del{j}_mp` | $b_i^- b_j^+$ |
172: | $-\delta_i - \delta_j$ ($i<j$) | `E_del{i}_del{j}_mm` | $b_i^- b_j^-$ |
173: 
174: The fermionic oscillator generators are labeled `a_1_p` ($a_1^+$) and `a_1_m` ($a_1^-$); bosonic oscillators retain labels `b_k_p`, `b_k_m`.
175: 
176: ---
177: 
178: ### 3. PBW Ordering — OPTIONS FOR HUMAN SELECTION
179: 
180: The PBW ordering determines how oscillator words are reduced to standard form in structure-constant computations. The even generator ordering (Cartan and $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$ part) is unambiguous and follows B(0,n):
181: 
182: ```
183: [Cartan: H_1, ..., H_{n+1}]
184: < [positive Sp: E_2del{k}_p (k=1..n), E_del{i}_del{j}_pp (i<j)]
185: < [negative Sp: E_2del{k}_m (k=1..n), E_del{i}_del{j}_mm (i<j)]
186: < [mixed Sp: E_del{i}_del{j}_pm (i<j), E_del{i}_del{j}_mp (i<j)]
187: ```
188: 
189: The key decision is how to order the **4n odd generators** relative to one another.
190: 
191: ---
192: 
193: #### **Option A — ε-first ordering** (group by ε-sign, then by k)
194: 
195: Oscillator word order: `a_1_p < a_1_m < b_1_p < b_1_m < b_2_p < b_2_m < ...`
196: 
197: All positive-ε generators come first, then negative-ε:
198: 
199: ```
200: PBW: [odd-pp: E_eps_del1_pp, ..., E_eps_deln_pp]
201:    < [odd-pm: E_eps_del1_pm, ..., E_eps_deln_pm]
202:    < [odd-mp: E_eps_del1_mp, ..., E_eps_deln_mp]
203:    < [odd-mm: E_eps_del1_mm, ..., E_eps_deln_mm]
204:    < [even]
205: ```
206: 
207: **For C(2) (n=1)**:
208: ```
209: E_eps_del1_pp < E_eps_del1_pm < E_eps_del1_mp < E_eps_del1_mm
210: < H_1, H_2, E_2del1_p, E_2del1_m
211: ```
212: 
213: **For C(3) (n=2)**:
214: ```
215: E_eps_del1_pp, E_eps_del2_pp
216: < E_eps_del1_pm, E_eps_del2_pm
217: < E_eps_del1_mp, E_eps_del2_mp
218: < E_eps_del1_mm, E_eps_del2_mm
219: < H_1, H_2, H_3, E_2del1_p, E_2del2_p, E_del1_del2_pp,
220:   E_2del1_m, E_2del2_m, E_del1_del2_mm,
221:   E_del1_del2_pm, E_del1_del2_mp
222: ```
223: 
224: **Rationale**: Directly reflects the oscillator-word PBW ordering (`a_1_p < a_1_m`). Consistent with how B(0,n) orders by the fermionic symbol first. Computationally natural for term-by-term reduction.
225: 
226: ---
227: 
228: #### **Option B — δ-first ordering** (group by k, then by ε-sign within each k)
229: 
230: All generators associated with bosonic index k are grouped together:
231: 
232: ```
233: PBW: [k=1: E_eps_del1_pp, E_eps_del1_pm, E_eps_del1_mp, E_eps_del1_mm]
234:    < [k=2: E_eps_del2_pp, E_eps_del2_pm, E_eps_del2_mp, E_eps_del2_mm]
235:    < ...
236:    < [k=n: E_eps_deln_pp, E_eps_deln_pm, E_eps_deln_mp, E_eps_deln_mm]
237:    < [even]
238: ```
239: 
240: **For C(2) (n=1)**:
241: ```
242: E_eps_del1_pp, E_eps_del1_pm, E_eps_del1_mp, E_eps_del1_mm
243: < H_1, H_2, E_2del1_p, E_2del1_m
244: ```
245: (Same as Option A for n=1; difference appears for n≥2.)
246: 
247: **For C(3) (n=2)**:
248: ```
249: E_eps_del1_pp, E_eps_del1_pm, E_eps_del1_mp, E_eps_del1_mm
250: < E_eps_del2_pp, E_eps_del2_pm, E_eps_del2_mp, E_eps_del2_mm
251: < H_1, H_2, H_3, E_2del1_p, E_2del2_p, E_del1_del2_pp,
252:   E_2del1_m, E_2del2_m, E_del1_del2_mm,
253:   E_del1_del2_pm, E_del1_del2_mp
254: ```
255: 
256: **Rationale**: Groups all roots involving $\delta_k$ together, making it easier to identify the subalgebra structure associated with each bosonic mode. Closer to a "physical" interpretation where each bosonic mode $b_k$ with its fermionic partners forms a block.
257: 
258: ---
259: 
260: ### Summary of Key Differences Between Options
261: 
262: | Property | Option A (ε-first) | Option B (δ-first) |
263: |---|---|---|
264: | Primary sort key | ε-sign of root | δ-index k |
265: | Oscillator word order | `a_1_p < a_1_m < b_k_p < b_k_m` | `b_1 < b_2 < ...` blocks |
266: | n=1 (C(2)) | Identical | Identical |
267: | n≥2 difference | All pp-type before any pm-type | All k=1 types before any k=2 |
268: | Analogy to B(0,n) | Closer (fermionic symbol first) | Root-index block structure |
269: 
270: **Recommendation**: Option A is more consistent with the B(0,n) convention and reflects the standard oscillator PBW reduction procedure. Option B may be preferable if the intent is to mirror the structure of the $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$ basis organization.
271:
